$comment: SHIPPED DEFAULT model floor for a fresh installation.
src/lib/model-floor.js reads this file at load and src/lib/tool-registry.js
refuses a delegated run whose model is not on it, so it has to ship. The
builder's own copy is not the file to ship, and the reason is not that it
contains a secret -- it does not. It contains their WORKING NOTES: their
instructions quoted verbatim and attributed, an argument about how two of
those instructions interact, dated incident write-ups naming which internal
lane made which mistake, the names of the agents who own each file, and a
declaration-site index describing a repository the installer does not have.
Publishing someone's private engineering correspondence inside a config file
is a privacy failure even when every individual sentence is harmless.
WHAT SURVIVES IS THE RULE ITSELF, unchanged and still enforced:
* purposesCannotLowerTheFloor stays true. The reader FAILS CLOSED if it is
anything else, and that refusal is the whole point: there is no lane type,
planning pass, review pass or advisory call that gets a cheaper model. A
per-purpose exception is how a floor stops being a floor.
* unknownIsRefusal stays true. An id that is not listed is refused whether
it is weaker, unknown, or merely unverified -- never assumed acceptable.
* A model below the floor is a REFUSAL, never a silent substitution to
something cheaper.
The model ids are public Google identifiers, not builder data, and are kept
so the floor is enforceable rather than empty on a fresh machine. refusedIds
keeps the ids and the technical reason, without the incident narrative.
declarationSites is absent. It indexes source files in the builder's working
tree and pins them against drift; the check that reads it does not ship, and a
shipped index of files that are not here would describe nothing. The reader
treats the field as optional.
A stronger model that is proven to serve is always addable here. That is the
one direction this file is meant to move.

subscription.$identity: The Gemini Code Assist account this installation is signed in to, if any.

vertex.$identity: A billed Vertex AI project this installation is configured for, if any.

notServable.gemini-2.5-flash: Not servable through the CLI lane path on Vertex: the CLI substitutes its own default flash id, which is not enabled on a Vertex project. The provider error would otherwise name a model nobody requested.

vertex-seat.$identity: A separately configured Vertex seat, if any.

refusedIds.gemini-3.6-flash: Not a real model id in the supported CLI, and a flash tier. A run launched with an id the CLI does not know cannot get the model that was asked for; the CLI substitutes something else without saying so.
refusedIds.gemini-3.5-flash: Below floor. A real id -- the CLI's default flash model -- but a flash tier.
refusedIds.gemini-2.5-flash: Below floor on every backend, and additionally not servable on Vertex through the CLI lane path.
refusedIds.gemini-3.1-flash-lite: Below floor. Observed being served silently in response to an explicit pro request, which is the silent downgrade this floor exists to catch.
refusedIds.gemini-3-flash-preview: Below floor. Observed being served in response to a requested pro model, caught by the serve-side check -- which is why checking the served model matters and checking only the requested one does not.
